content: This information does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your use. It is not intended to replace personalized medical advice and should not substitute for the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: This medication is typically administered by injection into a vein as directed by your doctor, usually every six hours. It should be injected slowly over a period of 20 to 60 minutes. This injectable medication should only be used until you are able to take an oral antibiotic or until your treatment is complete. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue using it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in the infection returning. If you are using this medication to prevent certain bacterial infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea or loose stools, stomach pain, or pain and redness at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other macrolide/ketolide antibiotics (such as clarithromycin or azithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Erythromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). It may also cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation, especially if you are using certain medications (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Infants may be at higher risk for a serious stomach condition. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Erythromycin passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of erythromycin from your body, which could impact how it works. Similarly, erythromycin may slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (such as urine tests), possibly causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Laboratory and/or medical tests may be conducted while you are using this medication. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for proper storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare provider. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
